name: Narmer's Unification of Egypt
description: Wars of unification of Upper and Lower Egypt traditionally credited to Narmer, founding the First Dynasty and the Egyptian state.

name: Weni's Campaigns against the Sand-Dwellers
description: Five campaigns under Pepi I led by the official Weni against the Aamu 'Sand-Dwellers' of the Sinai and southern Levant, one of the earliest narrated Egyptian wars.

name: First Intermediate Period Civil Wars
description: Series of civil wars between the Herakleopolitan and Theban dynasties ending with Mentuhotep II's reunification of Egypt.

name: Kamose's War against the Hyksos
description: Final Theban campaigns of Kamose against the Hyksos in the Nile Delta, recorded on the Carnarvon Tablet and Kamose Stelae.

name: Battle of Megiddo (15th century BCE)
description: Thutmose III's decisive victory over the Canaanite coalition led by the king of Kadesh, the first battle recorded in detail in history.

name: Egyptian-Mitanni Wars
description: Series of Thutmoside campaigns in Syria against the Mitanni Empire under Thutmose I, Thutmose III, and Amenhotep II.

name: Battle of Kadesh
description: Ramesses II's clash with Muwatalli II of Hatti, the largest chariot battle of antiquity and subject of the earliest known peace treaty.

name: Merneptah's Libyan War
description: Merneptah's defeat of a Libyan-Sea Peoples coalition in the western Delta, commemorated on the Merneptah Stele (which contains the earliest known mention of Israel).

name: Battle of the Delta
description: Naval battle in which Ramesses III repelled the Sea Peoples invasion in the eighth year of his reign.

name: Battle of Djahy
description: Land victory of Ramesses III over the Sea Peoples in the southern Levant, paired with the naval Battle of the Delta.

name: Kushite Conquest of Egypt
description: Piye and Shabaka's conquest of Egypt founding the Kushite 25th Dynasty (the 'Black Pharaohs').

name: Assyrian Conquest of Egypt
description: Esarhaddon's and Ashurbanipal's campaigns ending Kushite rule in Egypt, climaxing in the sack of Thebes (663 BC).

name: Battle of Carchemish
description: Nebuchadnezzar II's decisive defeat of Necho II's Egyptian forces, ending Egyptian ambitions in Syria.

name: Battle of Pelusium (525 BCE)
description: Cambyses II's victory over Psamtik III ending the 26th Dynasty and incorporating Egypt into the Persian Empire as the 27th Dynasty.

name: Egyptian Revolt of Inaros
description: Athenian-backed Libyan-Egyptian revolt against Persian rule, ending in catastrophic defeat at Prosopitis.

name: Battle of Pelusium (343 BCE)
description: Artaxerxes III's reconquest of Egypt, ending the last native Egyptian dynasty (Nectanebo II).

name: Alexander's Conquest of Egypt
description: Alexander the Great's bloodless conquest of Persian Egypt and foundation of Alexandria.

name: Syrian Wars
description: Six wars between Ptolemaic Egypt and the Seleucid Empire over control of Coele-Syria.

name: First Syrian War
description: First conflict between Ptolemy II and Antiochus I over Syria.

name: Second Syrian War
description: War of Ptolemy II against Antiochus II and Antigonus II Gonatas in Asia Minor and the Aegean.

name: Third Syrian War (Laodicean War)
description: Ptolemy III's expedition deep into Seleucid territory in support of his sister Berenice.

name: Fourth Syrian War
description: Ptolemy IV's war with Antiochus III, decided by the Battle of Raphia (217 BC), one of the largest battles of the Hellenistic age.

name: Battle of Raphia
description: Ptolemy IV's decisive victory over Antiochus III, the only major Seleucid defeat of Antiochus's reign.

name: Fifth Syrian War
description: Antiochus III's conquest of Coele-Syria from Ptolemy V, decided at the Battle of Panium.

name: Sixth Syrian War
description: Antiochus IV's invasion of Egypt halted by Roman intervention (the 'Day of Eleusis').

name: Great Revolt of the Egyptians
description: Twenty-year revolt of Upper Egypt under the native pharaohs Horwennefer and Ankhwennefer against Ptolemaic rule.

name: Mercenary War
description: Carthage's brutal war against its unpaid mercenaries and Libyan subjects after the First Punic War, narrated in Polybius.

name: Second Punic War
description: Hannibal's war against Rome, including the invasion of Italy via the Alps and Scipio's African campaign ending at Zama.

name: Punic Wars
description: Three-war umbrella encompassing the century-long Roman-Carthaginian struggle for the western Mediterranean.

name: Roman Conquest of Numidia
description: Caesar's African campaign against the Optimates and Juba I of Numidia, climaxing at Thapsus and annexing Numidia as Africa Nova.

name: Caesar's Civil War in Africa
description: North African theater of Caesar's civil war against the Pompeian senatorial faction allied with King Juba I.

name: Alexandrine War
description: Caesar's siege at Alexandria supporting Cleopatra VII against her brother Ptolemy XIII, including the burning of the Library.

name: Final War of the Roman Republic
description: Octavian's war against Mark Antony and Cleopatra VII, ending with the Battle of Actium and the Roman annexation of Egypt.

name: Battle of Actium
description: Naval battle in which Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra, paving the way for Roman annexation of Egypt.

name: Roman-Kushite War (Meroitic War)
description: Kandake Amanirenas's war against Roman Egypt, ending in the Treaty of Samos with favorable terms for Meroe.

name: Tacfarinas's War
description: Seven-year revolt of the Numidian chief Tacfarinas against Roman rule in Africa, drawing in the Garamantes.

name: Aedemon's Revolt
description: Mauretanian revolt following the murder of King Ptolemy of Mauretania by Caligula, suppressed by Suetonius Paulinus and Hosidius Geta.

name: Roman Expedition to the Garamantes
description: Cornelius Balbus's punitive expedition deep into the Fezzan against the Garamantes, the only Roman triumph awarded to a non-citizen.

name: Kitos War
description: Major Jewish diaspora revolt under Trajan, centered on Cyrene (Libya) and Egypt and suppressed at huge cost by Lusius Quietus.

name: Boukoloi Revolt
description: Revolt of the Boukoloi herdsmen of the Egyptian Delta under Marcus Aurelius, suppressed by Avidius Cassius (sometimes called the Bucolic War).

name: Domitius Domitianus Revolt
description: Revolt of Domitius Domitianus and Aurelius Achilleus in Egypt against Diocletian, ending with the eight-month siege of Alexandria.

name: Vandal Conquest of North Africa
description: Geiseric's Vandal-Alan invasion of Roman Africa, climaxing in the capture of Carthage (439) and founding the Vandal Kingdom.

name: Vandalic War
description: Belisarius's reconquest of North Africa from the Vandals under Justinian I, narrated by Procopius.

name: Moorish Wars (Byzantine)
description: Byzantine wars against Berber chieftains (notably Antalas, Cusina, and the Mauro-Roman kingdom) following the Vandal reconquest.

name: Stotzas's Mutiny
description: Major mutiny of the Byzantine African army under Stotzas, suppressed by Germanus and Belisarius.

name: Sasanian Conquest of Egypt
description: Khosrow II's general Shahrbaraz conquered Egypt from the Byzantines during the Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628.

name: Muslim Conquest of Egypt
description: Amr ibn al-As's conquest of Byzantine Egypt, including the Battle of Heliopolis and the sieges of Babylon and Alexandria.

name: Battle of Heliopolis
description: Decisive Arab victory under Amr ibn al-As over the Byzantine field army of Egypt.

name: Muslim Conquest of the Maghreb
description: Six-decade Arab conquest of the Maghreb under Abdallah ibn Sa'd, Uqba ibn Nafi, Hassan ibn al-Numan, and Musa ibn Nusayr.

name: Battle of Sufetula
description: First major Arab victory in Byzantine Africa, killing the exarch Gregory the Patrician.

name: Siege of Carthage (698)
description: Hassan ibn al-Numan's final capture and destruction of Byzantine Carthage, ending Roman rule in Africa.

name: Kahina's Berber Resistance
description: The Berber priestess-queen Dihya al-Kahina's resistance to the Arab conquest of the Maghreb, ending at the Battle of Tabarka.

name: Kusaila's Revolt
description: Berber chieftain Kusaila's revolt against the Arab conquest, killing Uqba ibn Nafi at the Battle of Vescera (683).

name: Berber Revolt
description: Kharijite Berber rebellion under Maysara al-Matghari that ended Umayyad control of the western Maghreb.

name: Battle of the Nobles
description: Crushing Berber Kharijite defeat of an Arab aristocratic army at Tangier, opening the Berber Revolt.

name: Battle of Bagdoura
description: Second great Berber victory of the Berber Revolt, annihilating Kulthum ibn Iyad's Syrian army.

name: Abbasid Conquest of Ifriqiya
description: Abbasid Muhallabid governors' reconquest of Ifriqiya from the Berber Kharijites.

name: Aghlabid Conquest of Sicily
description: Seventy-five-year Aghlabid conquest of Byzantine Sicily, establishing the Emirate of Sicily.

name: Fatimid Conquest of Ifriqiya
description: Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i's Kutama Berber campaign overthrowing the Aghlabids and Rustamids and founding the Fatimid Caliphate.

name: Abu Yazid's Revolt
description: Kharijite Berber revolt of 'the Man on the Donkey' that nearly toppled the Fatimid Caliphate before its suppression by al-Mansur.

name: Fatimid Conquest of Egypt
description: Jawhar al-Siqilli's bloodless conquest of Egypt for the Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz, founding the city of Cairo.

name: Qarmatian Invasions of Egypt
description: Qarmatian invasions of newly-conquered Fatimid Egypt, repelled by Jawhar al-Siqilli outside Cairo.

name: Banu Hilal Invasion
description: Mass Arab Bedouin migration into the Maghreb sent by the Fatimids to punish the Zirids, fundamentally Arabizing North Africa.

name: Battle of Haydaran
description: Catastrophic Zirid defeat by the Banu Hilal that opened Ifriqiya to Arab nomadic settlement.

name: Almoravid Conquest of the Maghreb
description: Yusuf ibn Tashfin and the Sanhaja Berber Almoravids' conquest of Morocco and the central Maghreb from Marrakech (founded 1070).

name: Almoravid Conquest of Ghana
description: Disputed but traditionally dated Almoravid southern campaigns from Sijilmasa under Abu Bakr ibn Umar, traditionally credited with sacking Kumbi Saleh.

name: Almohad Conquest of the Maghreb
description: Ibn Tumart's and Abd al-Mu'min's Masmuda Berber revolution overthrowing the Almoravids and unifying North Africa.

name: Norman Conquest of Mahdia
description: Roger II of Sicily's establishment of the short-lived Norman Kingdom of Africa along the Ifriqiyan coast, ended by Almohad reconquest.

name: Crusader Invasions of Egypt
description: Five campaigns of Amalric of Jerusalem and Shirkuh of Aleppo over Fatimid Egypt, ending with Saladin's rise.

name: Saladin's Conquest of Egypt
description: Saladin's seizure of power as Fatimid vizier and abolition of the Fatimid Caliphate, founding the Ayyubid dynasty.

name: Seventh Crusade
description: Louis IX's invasion of Egypt, capturing Damietta but defeated and captured at Mansurah and Fariskur.

name: Mamluk-Ilkhanid Wars
description: Six-decade Mamluk-Mongol struggle for Syria, defining the eastern frontier of Mamluk Egypt.

name: Battle of Ain Jalut
description: Qutuz and Baybars's defeat of the Mongols, halting the westward Mongol expansion and securing Mamluk Egypt.

name: Marinid Conquest of Morocco
description: Zenata Berber Marinid conquest of Almohad Morocco, capturing Marrakech in 1269.

name: Hafsid-Aragonese Wars
description: Aragonese maritime expeditions and tribute wars against the Hafsid sultans of Tunis, including the Sicilian Vespers' aftermath.

name: Battle of Rio Salado
description: Decisive Castilian-Portuguese victory over the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan, ending Moroccan ambitions in Iberia.

name: Mahdia Crusade
description: Franco-Genoese expedition against the Barbary pirate port of Mahdia, the last major crusade against Muslim North Africa.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Ceuta
description: John I of Portugal's capture of Ceuta, traditionally considered the beginning of the Portuguese overseas empire.

name: Tangier Disaster
description: Portuguese expedition led by Henry the Navigator and Prince Ferdinand the Saint, defeated outside Tangier.

name: Funj Conquest of Alodia
description: Funj founder Amara Dunqas's destruction of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alodia and foundation of the Sennar Sultanate.

name: Portuguese-Moroccan Wars
description: Three-and-a-half centuries of Portuguese coastal occupations and Moroccan reconquests, from Ceuta (1415) to Mazagan (1769).

name: Battle of Alcacer Quibir (Battle of the Three Kings)
description: Catastrophic Portuguese defeat in which King Sebastian I died, triggering the Iberian Union and consolidating Saadi power.

name: Spanish Conquest of Melilla
description: Castilian seizure of Melilla under Pedro de Estopiñán, beginning Spanish Plazas de Soberanía on the Moroccan coast.

name: Spanish Conquest of Oran
description: Cardinal Cisneros's expedition capturing Oran, part of the Spanish offensive into the Maghreb after the fall of Granada.

name: Algiers Expedition (1541)
description: Charles V's disastrous amphibious expedition against Hayreddin Barbarossa's Algiers, wrecked by storm.

name: Tunis Expedition (1535)
description: Charles V's amphibious capture of Tunis and La Goletta from Hayreddin Barbarossa, restoring the Hafsid Muley Hassan as vassal.

name: Conquest of Tunis (1574)
description: Sinan Pasha's Ottoman conquest ending Hafsid rule and the Spanish presidio at La Goletta, completing Ottoman control of the Maghreb.

name: Battle of Djerba
description: Devastating Ottoman naval victory over a Spanish-led Christian fleet under Giovanni Andrea Doria, off the Tunisian coast.

name: Siege of Malta (1565)
description: Ottoman siege of Malta launched from North African bases, repelled by the Knights of St. John under La Valette.

name: Capture of Mahdia (1550)
description: Spanish-Knights of Malta capture of the Ottoman corsair base of Mahdia from Turgut Reis.

name: Battle of Lepanto
description: Holy League's destruction of the Ottoman fleet, with major Algerian corsair participation under Uluj Ali.

name: Saadi Conquest of Songhai
description: Ahmad al-Mansur's trans-Saharan expedition under Judar Pasha that destroyed the Songhai Empire at the Battle of Tondibi.

name: Moroccan Civil War (1603-1627)
description: Succession war among the sons of Ahmad al-Mansur that fractured the Saadi state and gave rise to the Republic of Salé.

name: Alawi Conquest of Morocco
description: Moulay al-Rashid and Moulay Ismail's reunification of Morocco from Tafilalt, founding the still-ruling Alawi dynasty.

name: Anglo-Moroccan Wars (Tangier)
description: English occupation of Tangier (acquired in Catherine of Braganza's dowry) and its eventual abandonment under Moulay Ismail's siege.

name: French Bombardments of Algiers
description: Three French naval bombardments of Algiers under Duquesne and d'Estrées to suppress Barbary piracy.

name: Ottoman-Hotaki War in Egypt
description: Cairo's Great Insurrection of 1711, a violent factional war between Mamluk-Janissary factions in Ottoman Egypt.

name: Algerian-Tunisian Wars
description: Series of wars between the Ottoman Regency of Algiers and Husainid Tunis, most notably in 1735 and 1756.

name: Spanish-Algerian War (1775)
description: Spanish naval expeditions under O'Reilly (1775) and Barceló (1783-84) against Algiers, ending in Spanish defeat.

name: Mamluk-Ottoman War (1768-74)
description: Ali Bey al-Kabir's revolt declaring Egyptian independence and invading Ottoman Syria with Zahir al-Umar.

name: French Campaign in Egypt and Syria
description: Napoleon's invasion of Egypt, including the Battle of the Pyramids, the Battle of the Nile, and the Acre campaign.

name: Battle of the Pyramids
description: Napoleon's decisive defeat of the Mamluk cavalry of Murad Bey within sight of the Pyramids of Giza.

name: Battle of the Nile
description: Nelson's destruction of the French Mediterranean fleet in Aboukir Bay, stranding Napoleon's army in Egypt.

name: Cairo Revolts (1798-1800)
description: Two major Cairene revolts (October 1798, March-April 1800) against French occupation, suppressed by Kléber and Menou.

name: First Barbary War
description: U.S. naval war against the Tripolitanian pasha Yusuf Karamanli, including the Battle of Derna ('to the shores of Tripoli').

name: Second Barbary War
description: Decatur's U.S. naval expedition against the Dey of Algiers ending tribute payments by the United States.

name: Bombardment of Algiers (1816)
description: Anglo-Dutch naval bombardment under Lord Exmouth forcing the Dey of Algiers to free Christian slaves.

name: Egyptian Conquest of Sudan
description: Muhammad Ali's invasion of Sudan under Ismail Kamil Pasha and Mahu Bey, founding Turco-Egyptian Sudan (Turkiyya).

name: Greek War of Independence (Egyptian Phase)
description: Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian expeditionary force in Crete and the Peloponnese, destroyed at the Battle of Navarino.

name: First Egyptian-Ottoman War
description: Ibrahim Pasha's invasion of Syria for his father Muhammad Ali, threatening Istanbul and forcing Ottoman concessions at Kutahya.

name: Second Egyptian-Ottoman War
description: Renewed Egyptian-Ottoman war ended by European intervention, fixing Muhammad Ali's hereditary rule of Egypt at its present borders.

name: Battle of Nezib
description: Ibrahim Pasha's decisive defeat of the Ottoman army under Hafiz Pasha, threatening the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire.

name: Wahhabi War
description: Muhammad Ali's Egyptian campaigns against the First Saudi State on Ottoman commission, destroying Diriyah in 1818.

name: French Conquest of Algeria
description: Seven-decade French conquest beginning with the 1830 landing at Sidi Ferruch and ending with the conquest of the Saharan oases.

name: Invasion of Algiers (1830)
description: Charles X's amphibious expedition under Bourmont capturing Algiers and ending the Ottoman Regency.

name: Abd al-Qadir's Resistance
description: Emir Abd al-Qadir's fifteen-year jihad against the French conquest of western Algeria, ending in his surrender to Lamoricière.

name: Siege of Constantine
description: Two French sieges of Ahmad Bey's capital, the second of which captured Constantine and ended the eastern beylik.

name: First Franco-Moroccan War
description: Short Franco-Moroccan war provoked by Moroccan support for Abd al-Qadir, decided at the Battle of Isly.

name: Battle of Isly
description: Bugeaud's victory over Moroccan crown prince Sidi Muhammad, ending the First Franco-Moroccan War.

name: Bombardment of Tangier (1844)
description: Prince de Joinville's bombardment of Tangier opening the First Franco-Moroccan War.

name: Bombardment of Mogador
description: French naval bombardment and brief occupation of the Moroccan port of Mogador (Essaouira).

name: Hispano-Moroccan War
description: O'Donnell's Spanish expedition capturing Tetouan and forcing the Treaty of Wad-Ras with a large indemnity.

name: Kabyle Insurrection of 1871 (Mokrani Revolt)
description: Massive Kabyle revolt under Cheikh Mokrani and Cheikh El-Haddad, the largest indigenous uprising of French Algeria.

name: Bou Amama Insurrection
description: Long-running Saharan resistance to French rule led by Cheikh Bou Amama in southwestern Algeria and eastern Morocco.

name: Urabi Revolt
description: Egyptian army officer revolt against Khedive Tewfik and European financial control, triggering the British invasion of Egypt.

name: Battle of Tell el-Kebir
description: Garnet Wolseley's night attack destroying Urabi Pasha's entrenched army, ending the Anglo-Egyptian War.

name: Bombardment of Alexandria (1882)
description: Royal Navy bombardment of Alexandria's forts opening the Anglo-Egyptian War.

name: French Protectorate of Tunisia (Establishment)
description: French invasion and Treaty of Bardo establishing the French protectorate over Tunisia.

name: Sfax Insurrection
description: Tunisian popular insurrection against the French protectorate, suppressed by the capture of Sfax and Kairouan.

name: Mahdist Conquest of Sudan
description: Muhammad Ahmad al-Mahdi's revolt ending Turco-Egyptian rule of Sudan, climaxing in the fall of Khartoum (1885).

name: Siege of Khartoum
description: Ten-month Mahdist siege of Khartoum culminating in the city's fall and Gordon's death.

name: Hicks Expedition
description: Annihilation of William Hicks's Egyptian army at the Battle of El Obeid (Shaykan), the worst British-led defeat in Sudan.

name: Nile Expedition (Gordon Relief)
description: Wolseley's overland and riverine expedition to relieve Gordon at Khartoum, arriving two days after the city's fall.

name: Mahdist-Ethiopian Wars
description: Border wars in which the Mahdists sacked Gondar (1887) and killed Emperor Yohannes IV at the Battle of Gallabat (1889).

name: Battle of Gallabat (Metemma)
description: Mahdist defeat of an Ethiopian army in which Emperor Yohannes IV was killed.

name: Anglo-Egyptian Reconquest of Sudan
description: Kitchener's reconquest culminating at the Battle of Omdurman (1898) and the killing of the Khalifa at Umm Diwaykarat (1899).

name: Battle of Omdurman
description: Kitchener's annihilation of the Khalifa Abdallahi's army outside Omdurman, the most famous battle of the Mahdist War.

name: Fashoda Incident
description: Anglo-French confrontation on the upper Nile between Kitchener and Marchand, narrowly averting war over Sudan.

name: French Conquest of the Sahara
description: Two-decade French conquest of the Algerian and central Sahara, including the Flatters expeditions and the Battle of Tit.

name: Flatters Expeditions
description: Two French trans-Saharan railway-survey expeditions, the second of which was destroyed by the Hoggar Tuareg.

name: Battle of Tit
description: Cottenest's victory over the Kel Ahaggar Tuareg breaking organized Saharan resistance in the central Sahara.

name: First Moroccan Crisis
description: Diplomatic crisis sparked by Wilhelm II's visit to Tangier, resolved at the Algeciras Conference.

name: Agadir Crisis
description: German gunboat Panther's deployment to Agadir during the French occupation of Fez, prelude to the French Protectorate.

name: French Conquest of Morocco
description: Quarter-century French pacification of Morocco from the 1907 Casablanca landing through the 1934 Anti-Atlas campaigns.

name: Bombardment of Casablanca (1907)
description: French naval bombardment and occupation of Casablanca following anti-European riots.

name: Zaian War
description: Seven-year French campaign against the Zaian Berber confederation under Mouha ou Hammou Zayani in the Middle Atlas.

name: Battle of El Herri
description: Zaian destruction of Lieutenant-Colonel Laverdure's column, the worst French defeat of the Moroccan campaigns.

name: Hispano-Moroccan War (1893 / Margallo)
description: Margallo War or Melillan campaign, a Spanish punitive expedition after Riffian attacks on Melilla.

name: Second Melillan Campaign
description: Spanish campaign in the Rif following the Wolf Gully ambush, sparking Barcelona's Tragic Week.

name: Italo-Turkish War
description: Italian invasion of Ottoman Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, ending with the Treaty of Ouchy and the founding of Italian Libya.

name: Senussi Campaign (WWI)
description: Senussi-Ottoman attack from Cyrenaica into British-held western Egypt during World War I.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 1919
description: Nationwide Egyptian uprising against British rule led by the Wafd, leading to the 1922 unilateral declaration of independence.

name: Tripolitanian Republic War
description: Short-lived Arab republic in Tripolitania (al-Jumhuriya al-Trabulsiya), suppressed by the Italian 'Reconquista' under Volpi.

name: Italian Pacification of Libya
description: Italian reconquest of Cyrenaica and the Fezzan under Graziani featuring concentration camps, ending with Omar al-Mukhtar's execution.

name: Battle of Annual
description: Abd el-Krim's annihilation of Silvestre's Spanish army (~13,000 dead), the catalyst for the Rif War.

name: Alhucemas Landing
description: Major Franco-Spanish amphibious landing in the heart of the Rif, generally cited as the model for later WWII landings.

name: Ifni War
description: Hispano-Moroccan war in Ifni and the Spanish Sahara that ended with the Treaty of Angra de Cintra ceding Tarfaya to Morocco.

name: Sand War
description: Brief border war between Morocco and newly-independent Algeria over the southwestern frontier, mediated by the OAU.

name: Suez Crisis
description: Tripartite Anglo-French-Israeli invasion of Egypt following Nasser's nationalization of the Suez Canal.

name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War (Egyptian Front)
description: Egyptian invasion of Palestine and operations in the Negev, ending in the Faluja Pocket and the Rhodes Armistice.

name: Six-Day War
description: Israeli preemptive war seizing Sinai, Gaza, the Golan, and the West Bank from Egypt, Syria, and Jordan.

name: War of Attrition
description: Static Egyptian-Israeli artillery and air war along the Suez Canal following the Six-Day War.

name: Yom Kippur War (Sinai Front)
description: Egyptian crossing of the Suez Canal and the subsequent Israeli counterattack across to the African side at the Battle of the Chinese Farm.

name: Libyan-Egyptian War
description: Four-day border war between Gaddafi's Libya and Sadat's Egypt over Egypt's outreach to Israel.

name: Chadian-Libyan War
description: Decade-long Libyan intervention in Chad, ending with the 'Toyota War' and Chadian victory at Ouadi Doum and Aouzou.

name: Toyota War
description: Final phase of the Chadian-Libyan war featuring Chadian Toyota technicals defeating Libyan armor.

name: US-Libya Conflict (Gulf of Sidra)
description: Series of confrontations in the Gulf of Sidra including 1981 and 1989 air engagements and the 1986 Operation El Dorado Canyon bombing.

name: Operation El Dorado Canyon
description: US airstrikes against Libya ordered by Reagan in retaliation for the Berlin discotheque bombing.

name: Western Sahara War
description: Sixteen-year war between the Polisario Front and Morocco/Mauritania over the former Spanish Sahara, ending with a UN ceasefire.

name: Green March
description: Hassan II's mass civilian march into the Spanish Sahara forcing the Madrid Accords and the partition of the territory.

name: Algerian Civil War
description: Eleven-year war between the Algerian state and Islamist insurgents (FIS, GIA, GSPC) following the cancelled 1991 elections.

name: Black Decade Massacres
description: Wave of mass village massacres in Algeria's Mitidja region during the civil war (Rais, Bentalha, Sidi Hamed, etc.).

name: Insurgency in the Maghreb (AQIM)
description: Long-running low-intensity insurgency by al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb across the Algerian Sahara and the Sahel.

name: First Libyan Civil War
description: Anti-Gaddafi revolution with NATO air support that overthrew the Jamahiriya and killed Gaddafi at Sirte.

name: NATO Intervention in Libya
description: UN-authorized NATO operation (Unified Protector) enforcing a no-fly zone and supporting Libyan rebels.

name: Second Libyan Civil War
description: Six-year war between Tripoli-based GNA and Haftar's eastern LNA, with major foreign intervention.

name: Libyan Crisis (2011-present)
description: Umbrella term covering the First and Second Libyan Civil Wars and the intervening 2011-14 transitional period.

name: ISIL Insurgency in Libya
description: ISIL's seizure and loss of Derna and Sirte during the Second Libyan Civil War.

name: Battle of Sirte (2016)
description: Six-month GNA offensive (Operation Solid Structure) backed by US airstrikes that retook Sirte from ISIL.

name: Sinai Insurgency
description: Ongoing jihadist insurgency in the Sinai Peninsula, escalating into a major insurgency after 2013.

name: Rabaa Massacre
description: Egyptian security forces' dispersal of Muslim Brotherhood sit-ins after Morsi's overthrow, killing hundreds in a single day.

name: First Sudanese Civil War
description: Seventeen-year war between the Khartoum government and southern Anyanya rebels, ending with the Addis Ababa Agreement.

name: Second Sudanese Civil War
description: Twenty-two-year war between Khartoum and John Garang's SPLA ending with the Comprehensive Peace Agreement and the path to South Sudanese independence.

name: War in Darfur
description: Genocidal counter-insurgency war in western Sudan between Khartoum/Janjaweed and Darfuri rebel movements (SLA, JEM).

name: South Kordofan Conflict
description: Sudanese government war against SPLM-North in South Kordofan and Blue Nile after South Sudan's independence.

name: Sudanese Revolution
description: Mass protests overthrowing Omar al-Bashir after thirty years in power, leading to a transitional government.

name: Sudan Civil War (2023-present)
description: Ongoing civil war between the SAF and Hemedti's RSF, displacing over 10 million Sudanese.

name: Tuareg Rebellion (1962-64)
description: First Tuareg insurrection in newly-independent Mali in the Adrar des Ifoghas.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 1952
description: Free Officers' coup under Naguib and Nasser overthrowing King Farouk and ending the Muhammad Ali dynasty.

name: Anti-British Insurgency in the Canal Zone
description: Egyptian fedayeen attacks on British forces in the Suez Canal Zone, precipitating Black Saturday and the 1952 Revolution.

name: North Yemen Civil War (Egyptian Intervention)
description: Egypt's eight-year intervention in Yemen on behalf of the republicans, often called 'Nasser's Vietnam.'

name: Tunisian Revolution
description: Self-immolation of Mohamed Bouazizi sparking nationwide protests that toppled Ben Ali, igniting the Arab Spring.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
description: Eighteen days of protests centered on Tahrir Square that overthrew Hosni Mubarak after thirty years in power.

name: Egyptian Coup d'État of 2013
description: Military overthrow of Mohamed Morsi by Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, ending the post-2011 democratic experiment.

name: Polisario Insurgency (post-2020)
description: Resumption of low-intensity warfare between Morocco and the Polisario Front after the 2020 Guerguerat incident ended the 29-year ceasefire.

name: Hyksos Conquest of Egypt
description: Gradual takeover of Lower Egypt by Levantine Hyksos rulers, founding the 15th Dynasty at Avaris.

name: Ramesside Asian Campaigns
description: Asiatic campaigns of Seti I and Ramesses II in the Levant, including the Battle of Kadesh and Egyptian-Hittite peace treaty.

name: Persian Reconquest of Egypt (Artaxerxes III)
description: Final Achaemenid reconquest of Egypt under Artaxerxes III, ending native Egyptian rule.

name: Khurshid Pasha's Revolt
description: Power struggle in post-French Egypt between Ottoman pashas, Mamluk beys, and Albanian troops, ending with Muhammad Ali's rise.

name: Massacre of the Mamluks
description: Muhammad Ali's ambush and slaughter of the Mamluk beys at Cairo Citadel, consolidating his rule of Egypt.

name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan Pacification
description: Quarter-century of campaigns consolidating Anglo-Egyptian rule including the conquest of Darfur (1916).

name: Anglo-Egyptian Conquest of Darfur
description: Anglo-Egyptian campaign annexing Sultan Ali Dinar's Darfur to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan during World War I.

name: Battle of the Mareth Line
description: Eighth Army's breach of the Axis Mareth Line in southern Tunisia during the Tunisian Campaign.

name: Operation Torch
description: Anglo-American invasion of French Morocco and Algeria, the first major US ground action in the western theater of WWII.

name: Tunisian Campaign
description: Final phase of the North African Campaign, including Kasserine Pass and the Allied victory at Cape Bon.

name: Battle of El Alamein
description: Montgomery's decisive Eighth Army victory over Rommel's Afrika Korps, the turning point of the North African Campaign.

name: Western Desert Campaign
description: Three-year see-saw campaign in Cyrenaica and the Egyptian western desert between the Commonwealth and the Axis.

name: Italian Invasion of Egypt
description: Graziani's brief invasion of Egypt from Libya, halted at Sidi Barrani and rolled back by Operation Compass.

name: Operation Compass
description: First major British offensive of the Western Desert campaign, destroying the Italian Tenth Army at Beda Fomm.

name: Siege of Tobruk
description: Eight-month Australian-led defense of Tobruk against Rommel's Afrika Korps, the longest siege in British military history.

name: Battle of Kasserine Pass
description: Rommel's tactical victory over green American troops in central Tunisia, prompting Eisenhower's command reforms.

name: Second Egyptian-Saudi War (Frontier War)
description: Muhammad Ali's renewed Egyptian campaign in central Arabia under Khurshid Pasha against the Second Saudi State.

name: Conquest of Songhai (Aftermath)
description: Decades of insurgency by Songhai successor states and Tuareg raids against the Moroccan-installed Pashalik of Timbuktu.

name: Moroccan-Spanish War of 1774
description: Sultan Muhammad III's hundred-day siege of Spanish Melilla, ending in Moroccan withdrawal.

name: Bombardment of Algiers (1683-1688)
description: Duquesne's bomb-vessel attacks on Algiers introducing mortar bombardment as a tool of European naval power.

name: Anglo-Sudan War (Suakin)
description: British expeditions on the Red Sea coast under Graham against Osman Digna's Beja forces, including the battles of El Teb and Tamai.

name: Battle of Adwa (Italian theater)
description: Decisive Ethiopian victory over the Italians in Tigray, ending the First Italo-Ethiopian War and inspiring anti-colonial movements.

name: Italian Conquest of the Fezzan
description: Final Italian campaigns in southern Libya including Graziani's capture of Kufra (1931).

name: First Egyptian-Saudi War
description: Tusun Pasha's and Ibrahim Pasha's seven-year Egyptian war against the First Saudi State, destroying Diriyah.

name: Tijaniyya Jihad of al-Hajj Umar (Saharan Phase)
description: Saharan-Sahelian jihad of al-Hajj Umar Tall founding the Toucouleur Empire across modern Mali, Senegal, and Mauritania.

name: Ma al-Aynayn's Resistance
description: Sheikh Ma al-Aynayn's anticolonial resistance in the Western Sahara and southern Morocco, suppressed at Tadla.

name: Mauritanian Pacification
description: Three-decade French conquest of the Saharan emirates (Trarza, Brakna, Tagant, Adrar), ending with the suppression of the Reguibat in the Zemmour.

name: Battle of Coulet (Coppolani's Assassination)
description: Assassination of French Mauritanian governor Xavier Coppolani by Tagant tribesmen, briefly halting French expansion.

name: Black Saturday (Cairo Fire)
description: Anti-British and anti-foreign riots that burned much of central Cairo, hastening the 1952 Revolution.

name: Polisario-Mauritanian War
description: Polisario campaign against Mauritanian-occupied southern Western Sahara, ending with the Mauritanian withdrawal after the 1978 coup.

name: Operation Black Buck / Suez airlift
description: U.S. emergency airlift of military supplies to Israel during the Yom Kippur War.

name: Sahrawi Intifada (2005)
description: Sahrawi civil-resistance protests in the Moroccan-administered Western Sahara, sometimes called the 'Independence Intifada.'

name: Gafsa Raid
description: Libyan-backed armed incursion into the Tunisian mining town of Gafsa, suppressed within days.

name: Battle of Amgala (1976)
description: Brief but consequential clash between Moroccan and Algerian regular forces inside Western Sahara at the war's outset.

name: 1989 Berber Spring
description: Kabyle protests against the suppression of Berber culture in Algeria, generally treated as protests rather than war but a notable conflict episode.

name: Black Spring (Kabylia 2001)
description: Kabyle unrest in northern Algeria following the killing of Massinissa Guermah, resulting in over 120 deaths.

name: Hirak Movement (Algeria)
description: Mass weekly protests forcing the resignation of Abdelaziz Bouteflika after twenty years in power.
